profile_reason: size l, tone critical → thorough (revise review, applied without re-review)

findings.title: Base branch refs created "in the job tree" are shared by all concurrent jobs
findings.detail: Step 3 says: "In the job tree, create `refs/heads/<name>` at `base.sha`, and also `refs/remotes/origin/<rest>`". The job tree is a `git worktree add` of the shared bare cache `repos/<repo_key>.git`. In git only HEAD, refs/bisect/* and refs/worktree/* are per-worktree. `refs/heads/*` and `refs/remotes/*` live in the common repo. If two jobs for the same repo run at once (the worker has several gate slots, or two coordinators send jobs), both write `refs/heads/main`. If their base shas differ, one job's `git merge-base $NW_BASE HEAD` resolves against the other job's base. That gives wrong affected-test selection or a wrong diff with no error. Step 6 also never deletes these refs, so the next job inherits a stale `main`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the worktree-per-job checkout with a private repo per job that borrows the cache's objects. Write step 3 as: "`git clone --shared --no-checkout repos/<repo_key>.git <job>/tree` (the objects are read through alternates; refs are private to the job), then `git -C <job>/tree checkout --detach <commit>`, then create `refs/heads/<name>` (and `refs/remotes/origin/<rest>` when `name` is `origin/<rest>`) at `base.sha` inside `<job>/tree`." Change step 6 to "`rm -rf <job>/tree`" in place of `git worktree remove --force`. Add an acceptance criterion: "Two concurrent gate-jobs for the same repo_key with different `base.sha` for the same `base.name` each see their own base in `git rev-parse $NW_BASE`."
findings.acceptance: The Design no longer writes branch refs into the shared cache. An AC and a test case cover two concurrent jobs with different bases.

findings.section: Design › Worker store / gate-job steps / gc
findings.title: Concurrency on the shared cache and have.json is unspecified
findings.detail: Several jobs can run at once on one worker, one per gate slot. Each one `git fetch`es into the same bare repo, sets `refs/nw/have/*` and updates `repos/<repo_key>.have.json`, and step 6 "run[s] `gc`" after every job. The spec has no lock. The read-modify-write of have.json races and can lose last-used times, so `gc` then ages refs out early. A `gc` triggered by job A can delete job B's in-flight `jobs/<job_id>/` (manual `gc --keep-days 0` certainly will) and its refs. Concurrent fetches into one repo can also fail on ref-lock contention.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Design › Worker store: "Each repo cache has a lock file `repos/<repo_key>.lock` (fcntl.flock). The bundle fetch, setting `refs/nw/have/*`, updating `<repo_key>.have.json` (written via temp file and os.replace) and `gc`'s deletions all happen under it. `gc` never deletes a job dir whose `job.lock` is flock-held by a live gate-job; every gate-job holds `jobs/<job_id>/job.lock` from claim until exit." Add a test: `gc --keep-days 0` run while a `sleep` gate job is live leaves that job's dir intact.
findings.acceptance: The spec names the lock and the in-flight-job exemption from gc, and a test covers gc during a live job.

findings.title: gc never prunes objects, so the cache grows without bound
findings.detail: `nw worker gc` "deletes job dirs and `refs/nw/have/*` refs older than N days". Deleting a ref does not free its objects. Nothing runs `git gc --prune` or `git worktree prune` (if worktrees stay). Every bundle's objects accumulate in `repos/<repo_key>.git` forever, yet `info` reports `free_bytes` as if space were managed.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the gc bullet: "... then, under the repo lock, runs `git -C repos/<repo_key>.git gc --prune=now --quiet` for each repo whose refs changed (and `git worktree prune` if worktrees are kept)." Extend the gc acceptance criterion: "after `gc --keep-days 0`, `nw worker have` reports none of the job's shas and `git cat-file -e <commit>` fails in the cache."
findings.acceptance: gc's description includes object pruning, and the AC checks that the objects are gone.

findings.title: Header fields `timeout_s`, `have` and `attempt`, and the 'protocol major' check, have no defined worker behaviour
findings.detail: The header carries `timeout_s`, `have: [...]` and `attempt: 0`, and step 1 validates "protocol major". None of these is defined. It is unclear whether `timeout_s` bounds the whole job, including the slot wait and checkout, or whether only `payload.gate_budget_s` (used as the deadline) applies. The worker's use of `have` and `attempt` is unspecified. The schema string is `nw.job.v1`, and no `protocol` field exists to take a major from. An implementer will guess, and SPEC-0338 will depend on that guess.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bullet list under the header block: "`timeout_s`: the worker ignores it (it is the coordinator's own wall-clock budget); the gate deadline is `slot hold + payload.gate_budget_s`. `have`: informational, the shas the coordinator assumed present when it cut the bundle; the worker does not read it, and a missing prerequisite surfaces as `error` with `stage: \"checkout\"`. `attempt`: echoed into `job.json` only. Protocol check: `schema` must equal `nw.job.v1`; any other value gives `error` with `stage: \"validate\"`." Alternatively, drop the fields the worker does not need.
findings.acceptance: Every header field has a stated worker behaviour or is removed.

findings.title: The slot_wait test needs a 30 s wait that the subprocess test cannot shorten
findings.detail: `slot_wait` is "emitted once the wait passes 30 s". That is `gate_slots.WAIT_EVENT_S = 30.0`, a module constant (`gate_slots.py:25`). The test runs `nw worker gate-job` as a subprocess, so it cannot monkeypatch the constant. The "held worker slot gives slot_wait/started" case would take at least 30 s per run. The spec also does not say what happens on stdin EOF during the slot wait.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Design step 4: "The 30 s threshold is read from `NW_WORKER_SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_S` (default 30) so tests can lower it. `cancel_event` is passed as `stop=` to `gate_slots.acquire`, so EOF during the wait ends it, and the worker emits `done` with `interrupted: true` and no `started`." In the Test plan, set that variable to 0.5 for the held-slot case and add a case "EOF while waiting for the slot".
findings.acceptance: The held-slot test runs in seconds, and EOF during the slot wait is specified and tested.

findings.title: The forced command's per-subcommand option grammar is not enumerated
findings.detail: "the rest match that subcommand's option grammar" leaves the allowlist to the implementer, and this is the security boundary. The arguments of `have --repo KEY` are not charset-checked either, so `--repo ../../x` could address a path outside `repos/`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace that phrase with an explicit grammar: "`info` [`--json`]; `have` `--repo` <[A-Za-z0-9._-]+> <[0-9a-f]{40,64}>...; `gate-job` (no arguments); `gc` [`--keep-days` <[0-9]+>]. Any other token is refused." Also state that `have` itself validates `--repo` against the same charset as `repo_key`.
findings.acceptance: ssh-command's accepted argv grammar is listed literally, and the tests cover a `--repo ../x` refusal.

findings.section: Design › gate-job steps (5. Run each gate)
findings.title: Placeholder and environment sources are underspecified
findings.detail: "with placeholders from the worker's tree path" covers only `{worktree}`. `{base}` must be `base.name` (to match `gates.placeholders`), `{spec_id}` and `{campaign}` come from the header, and `NW_BASE` must equal `base.name`, not the sha. The spec also does not say whether gates inherit the worker process's own `os.environ` (PATH, HOME) on top of the allowlist.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the step to: "placeholders `{worktree: <job>/tree, base: base.name, spec_id: header.spec_id, campaign: header.campaign}`; env = the worker process's own environment, plus the allowlisted keys from the header, plus `NW_WORKTREE`, `NW_DATA_DIR`, `NW_CONFIG_DIR` and `tmp_env(<job>/tmp)`. The header's `NW_BASE`, if present, must equal `base.name`, else `error` with `stage: \"validate\"`."
findings.acceptance: Each placeholder and env key has a stated source.

findings.title: Exit codes for normal completion are not stated
findings.detail: Only "exit code 3" for an exception and 2 for ssh-command refusal are given. It is not stated whether gate-job exits 0 after a `done` with `ok: false`, or what it exits on a validate or claim error. The coordinator (SPEC-0338) needs these to tell a transport failure from a gate failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: "gate-job exits 0 after emitting `done` (whatever `ok` is, including `interrupted: true`), 3 after an `error` frame at any stage, and never exits without one of the two frames unless stdout is closed."
findings.acceptance: The exit codes are listed for done, error and interrupted.

findings.title: The docs acceptance criterion has no test plan entry
findings.detail: The AC "`docs/WORKFLOW.md` documents the mandatory dedicated user and the absolute-path key line" is not mentioned in the Test plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Test plan: "**Manual:** check that `docs/WORKFLOW.md` has a 'Remote gate worker' section stating the dedicated unprivileged user is mandatory and showing the `command=\"/home/user/.local/bin/nw worker ssh-command\",restrict` key line."
findings.acceptance: Every AC maps to a test plan line.

findings.detail: validate_header rejects a job_id or repo_key outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]+, gate names outside the same charset, kind != 'gate', a bad commit/base sha and a bad payload.seq. findings.title: gc --keep-days 0 can prune a job's objects if the job is claimed after gc has scanned the job dirs
findings.detail: gc() builds live_ids/live_shas from one scan of jobs/ without any repo lock. It then takes each repo lock and deletes every refs/nw/have/* ref that is not in live_shas and is at least keep_s old (keep_s is 0 here, so every ref qualifies), plus every job ref whose owner is not in live_ids, and then runs `git gc --prune=now`. A gate-job that claims and fetches after the scan has fresh have refs and job refs that this gc treats as orphans. Its commit and base objects are then pruned. If that happens between the fetch and the clone, the job fails with a checkout error. If it happens after the clone, the running gates hit missing objects through alternates. With the default --keep-days 2 the fresh have refs survive, so only an explicit keep-days 0 (or a coordinator that issues one) is exposed.

In both cases gates.terminate_all() never runs, so the gate's process group (for example a long pytest run) keeps running on the worker with no owner, and the job dir keeps tree/ until gc ages it out.

findings.title: Signal handler raises at arbitrary points before the slot stage; it can skip a lock release and deadlock the job's own cleanup
findings.detail: In the validate/claim/checkout stages on_signal raises WorkerError, which runs between any two bytecodes of the main thread. If it lands in the finally of repo_lock or jobs_lock, after the body but before fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_UN)/os.close(fd), the new exception replaces the unwind and the fd stays open and locked. _fail then calls _cleanup, which calls _drop_job_refs (repo_lock) and gc (jobs_lock, repo_lock). Each opens a new open file description and blocks with LOCK_EX against the leaked lock held by the same process, so the process hangs forever while holding the repo or jobs lock. Every other job for that repo, or every claim on the worker, then stalls.

findings.title: A signal during checkout SIGKILLs a running git, which can leave stale ref locks in the shared cache

Every later job naming that sha (often a shared base sha) then fails _set_have (check=True) with stage checkout until someone deletes the lock by hand. gc does not clean .lock files.

verdict.summary: SPEC-0336: pre-slot signals no longer raise inside a lock release or a running git, stale git lock files in the worker cache are cleared, and the concurrent-jobs test pins slots: 2. Before the slot stage, the signal handler only records a SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP. Every git that writes the cache runs under the repo lock, so checkout, have and gc now delete leftover git `.lock` files before they write.

findings.title: git fetch's detached auto-gc writes the cache outside the repo lock, so `_clear_stale_locks` can delete live git locks
findings.detail: `_checkout` runs `git -C cache fetch ... <bundle>` with no `--no-auto-maintenance`/`--no-auto-gc`, and the cache is created by a plain `git init --bare` with no `gc.auto=0`/`maintenance.auto=false`. By default git fetch runs `git maintenance run --auto` when it finishes. Once the cache passes `gc.autoPackLimit` (50 packs) or `gc.auto` (6700 loose objects), that becomes a `git gc --auto` that detaches into the background (gc/maintenance autoDetach is on by default). It keeps running after `_checkout` releases the repo lock. Each bundle fetch is unbundled through index-pack and adds a pack. The worker's own `gc()` only repacks when it removed refs, and that rarely happens within the 2-day keep window, because every job drops its own job refs before it calls gc. So on a busy worker, 50 jobs for one repo are enough to start a detached gc. This breaks the rule stated at worker.py:166-169 and in the spec ('every git that writes the cache runs under the repo lock, so a git lock file found while holding it is stale'). The next job, `have` or `gc` then deletes the detached gc's in-flight `packed-refs.lock` and `refs/**/*.lock` (pack-refs prune locks), so two writers act on the same refs. Other effects: the running gc's pack-refs fails; a concurrent `update-ref` (have refs, job-ref deletion) fails with 'unable to lock', which shows up as a `checkout` error or a silently orphaned job ref; and the explicit `git gc --prune=now` in `gc()` exits 'gc is already running' (check=False) while the repo is still listed in `pruned`, so the objects are not freed.
findings.trigger: About 50 gate jobs for one repo_key within the keep window (each bundle fetch adds a pack). The next fetch starts a detached `git gc --auto` in the cache. A concurrent job, `have` or `gc` then takes the repo lock and runs `_clear_stale_locks` while that gc holds packed-refs.lock or refs/*.lock.

findings.title: Gate processes inherit the job's stdin (the SSH channel), not /dev/null
findings.detail: `run_gate` starts gates with `Popen(..., stdout=log, stderr=STDOUT)` and no `stdin=`, so on the worker each gate inherits fd 0. That fd is the coordinator's still-open job pipe, which the `_watch_stdin` thread is also reading. A gate (or a tool it calls) that reads stdin, for example a prompt, `read`, or a test runner reading input, blocks until the gate timeout or until the coordinator ends the job. In a local run it would get EOF or a tty instead. Its reads also compete with the watcher for the cancel signal.
findings.trigger: A gate command that reads stdin, e.g. `read x` or a tool that prompts, run through `nw worker gate-job` over SSH.

findings.title: `gc` reports a repo as pruned even when `git gc --prune=now` failed
findings.detail: `_git(..., 'gc', '--prune=now', '--quiet', check=False)` ignores the return code, and `out['pruned'].append(key)` runs regardless. If the gc fails (for example 'gc is already running', see the finding above, or a full disk), the objects stay while the summary says the repo was pruned.
findings.trigger: `nw worker gc --keep-days 0` while another git gc holds the cache's gc.pid.

findings.title: A signal during the clone/checkout gives `done interrupted`, not the documented `error stage: signal`
findings.detail: `_checkout`'s last `stop.check()` runs before the clone, checkout and update-ref steps, and `gate_job` does not check again before it sets stage `slot`. Because `on_signal` has already set `cancel`, the job emits `accepted` and then `done` with interrupted true (exit 0). The spec says pre-slot signals end with `error` stage `signal` and exit 3, and lists 'after the checkout' as one of the check points.
findings.trigger: SIGTERM while `git clone --shared` or `git checkout --detach` is running in `_checkout`.

findings.title: Frames use ensure_ascii=False, so U+2028/U+0085 from gate output appear raw in a JSON-lines frame
findings.detail: `result.tail` (gate output) is placed raw in the `gate` frame. JSON does not escape U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085. A reader that splits with `str.splitlines()` instead of on b'\n' would split one frame into two.
findings.trigger: A gate whose last log lines contain U+2028 or NEL, read by a coordinator that uses splitlines().

verdict.fix_brief: Stop git from running maintenance in the worker cache on its own, so that the repo-lock rule `_clear_stale_locks` depends on actually holds. Add a test that runs a fetch on a cache with `gc.autoPackLimit=1` and asserts that no `gc.pid` or background gc is left after `_checkout` returns.

findings.title: Gate processes inherit the job-protocol stdin pipe
findings.detail: run_gate's Popen sets no stdin, so each gate inherits fd 0, which is the coordinator's job stream. That stream stays open until `done`. If a gate reads stdin (a `read`, a tool that prompts, `cat` with no file), it blocks until its own timeout_s instead of getting EOF at once as it would under a local run with stdin at /dev/null or a terminal. The stdin watcher reads the same fd at the same time. The spec records this as a known deviation, so this is hardening only.
findings.trigger: A gate cmd such as `python -c 'import sys; sys.stdin.read()'`, or a script that asks for input, hangs for the full timeout_s on the worker.

findings.title: Cache fetch needs git >= 2.29 and nothing checks for it
findings.detail: `--no-write-fetch-head` and `--no-auto-maintenance` arrived in git 2.29. On an older worker git, every job with a bundle fails at stage `checkout` with "unknown option". `info` reports the git version but nothing checks or documents a minimum. `--no-auto-maintenance` is also redundant now, because the cache config already sets gc.auto=0 and maintenance.auto=false.
findings.trigger: A worker host with git 2.25 (for example Ubuntu 20.04): every gate-job with bundle_bytes > 0 returns error stage `checkout`.

findings.title: Gate names `a` and `a.r1` collide on retry files
findings.detail: Unique-name validation does not stop one gate's stem from equalling another gate's retry stem. Gate `a` with retries writes `001-a.r1.log`/`.json`, which is the main log of a gate named `a.r1`. The retry regex in gate_files also attributes `001-a.r1.*` to gate `a`. Local runs share the same naming, so the cause predates this change, but the worker could reject such names in validation.
findings.trigger: payload.gates = [{name: 'a.r1', ...}, {name: 'a', retries: 1, cmd: 'false'}]: gate `a`'s frame carries `a.r1`'s files, and its retry overwrites them.

findings.title: NaN/Infinity gate_budget_s and NUL in env values get past validation
findings.detail: json.loads accepts NaN and Infinity, and `budget <= 0` is False for both, so the deadline becomes NaN or inf. Env values are only type-checked, so a NUL byte gets through and makes Popen raise ValueError after `started`. That gives an `error` frame with stage `slot` instead of a `validate` refusal.
findings.trigger: A header with `"gate_budget_s": NaN`, or env `{"NW_SPEC_ID": "a\u0000b"}`.

findings.title: gc --keep-days with an enormous value raises OverflowError
findings.detail: `now - keep_s` turns a huge int into a float and raises OverflowError. The forced-command grammar allows any number of digits.
findings.trigger: `nw worker gc --keep-days` followed by a 400-digit number prints a traceback.

verdict.summary:
SPEC-0336: gates now get /dev/null as stdin instead of the job stream, the cache fetch works on git older than 2.29, validation is stricter (non-finite budget, NUL bytes, gate names that collide with another gate's retry files), gc --keep-days is capped, and new tests cover the origin/main base, the budget deadline, worker env, have edge cases, SIGHUP and the docs.

Code changes in worker.py: the stdin watcher reads a private dup of the job fd, and fd 0 is replaced with /dev/null, so a gate that reads stdin gets EOF at once. The cache fetch no longer passes the git 2.29-only flags (the cache config already turns auto gc off). An origin/<rest> base sets core.warnAmbiguousRefs=false in the job tree so resolving it prints no ambiguity warning. Validation refuses NaN/Infinity gate_budget_s, NUL bytes in env values and in gate fields, and a gate named `<other gate>.r<n>`. gc caps --keep-days at 100000. I could not edit Design step 4 (the spec is guarded), so the slot campaign id `remote:<campaign>` is recorded in As shipped. The targeted set (184 tests) passed in all 12 repeat runs at -n 4/6/8, and the spec's test record says so. The loop 6 one-off failure did not recur, but its cause is still unidentified.

findings.title: One broken cache makes `nw worker gc` abort for every repo after it
findings.detail: Inside gc's per-repo loop, `_no_auto_maintenance(cache)` calls `_git(..., 'config', key, value)` with check=True. If that fails it raises WorkerError, which nothing catches. The CLI `nw worker gc` exits with a traceback, and the repos that sort after the broken one are never aged or pruned. The end-of-job `_cleanup` → `gc(cfg)` path catches the error but still skips the remaining repos. So a single damaged cache keeps every later cache from being bounded.
findings.trigger: `repos/<key>.git` has a HEAD but an unwritable or corrupt `config` (for example `git init --bare` killed hard, a full disk, or wrong permissions), and another repo key sorts after it.

findings.title: The base name is only fully checked after the fetch and have refs are written
findings.detail: BASE_RE plus the `..` check accept names that git's check-ref-format rejects: `main.lock`, `a//b`, a trailing `/`, `x/.y`, `@{`-free but invalid forms. `check-ref-format` only runs in `_checkout` after the bundle fetch, after `_set_have` and after the clone. The job then fails with stage `checkout` instead of `validate`, and by then it has already written the cache and the have refs. This is harmless today, but it breaks the 'nothing runs before validate passes' intent for this input.
findings.trigger: A header with `base.name` = `main.lock` or `feature/`.

findings.title: A signal between checkout and the slot stage gives `done` interrupted instead of an `error` with stage `signal`
findings.detail: Once `_checkout` returns, `state['stage']` stays `checkout` while the watcher thread starts. A signal in that window only records `stop.name` and sets `cancel`. No `stop.check()` runs before the stage changes to `slot`, so `acquire` returns an interrupted hold, and the job emits `accepted` followed by `done` interrupted and exits 0. The As-shipped notes say a pre-slot signal ends in `error` with stage `signal` and exit 3. The outcome is still a clean cancel, but the documented exit-code contract is not exact here.
findings.trigger: SIGTERM delivered right after `_checkout` returns and before `state['stage'] = 'slot'`.

findings.title: `info().git_sha` can report an unrelated repo's HEAD
findings.detail: `git -C <installed package dir> rev-parse HEAD` runs with the caller's environment unscrubbed (it does not use `_git_env`), and git walks up parent directories looking for a repo. If GIT_DIR is set, or a parent directory of the install is a git repo (for example a dotfiles-tracked home directory), the reported `git_sha` belongs to that other repo.
findings.trigger: A worker user whose home directory is a git repo, with nightwright installed via `uv tool install` under `~/.local/share/uv/tools/...`.

findings.title: The `job.lock` fd is never closed
findings.detail: `lock_fd` is opened and flocked in `gate_job`, and nothing ever closes it. Process exit releases it for the CLI. An in-process caller, such as the tests that call `gate_job` directly, keeps both the fd and the lock, so that job looks live to every later gc in the same process.
findings.trigger: Repeated in-process calls to `W.gate_job(...)`.

findings.title: A blocked frame write keeps the worker's gate slot held, and signals cannot interrupt it
findings.detail: `_Frames.emit` writes and flushes to stdout with no timeout, and it runs on the main thread inside `gate_slots.acquire` (gate frames can be about 16 MiB of base64 per file). A coordinator that stays connected but stops reading stdout fills the pipe, and the worker then blocks in `write` while holding its slot. From the `slot` stage on, `on_signal` only starts a `terminate_all` thread and does not raise. PEP 475 retries the interrupted write, so SIGTERM/SIGHUP cannot end the job either. The stdin watcher sets `cancel` on EOF, but the main thread never gets back to check it.
findings.trigger: A coordinator whose SSH session stays up but which stops draining stdout (for example, hung on a lock) while a gate frame larger than the pipe buffer is being written.

findings.title: Every job's exit waits on a global gc of all repo caches, which can include a full `git gc --prune=now`
findings.detail: `_cleanup` calls `gc(cfg)`, and `gc` walks every `repos/*.git`. For each one it takes that repo's lock, so it waits behind another repo's large bundle fetch. When any have ref has aged past 2 days, it also runs `git gc --prune=now` with no timeout. Have refs age continuously, so the first job to finish after each 2-day mark pays for a full repack of some cache. The process exits only afterwards, and the coordinator reads the exit code to tell transport failure from gate failure, so the job's end is delayed. Signals sent during this phase only start `terminate_all` threads and do not stop the process.
findings.trigger: A worker caching a large repo whose have refs are more than 2 days old: the next unrelated gate-job, for any repo, blocks its exit on `git gc --prune=now` of that cache after emitting `done`.

findings.title: `job_id` `.` or `..` passes validation and is refused at `claim` instead of `validate`
findings.detail: `KEY_RE` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`) accepts `.` and `..`. `jobs_dir / '..'` is the existing `worker/` dir, so `mkdir` raises FileExistsError and the job is reported as a duplicate (`stage: claim`) even though no such job exists. Nothing escapes the store, but the error stage is misleading. The same names are also accepted as `repo_key`/`campaign`, where the appended suffixes produce odd file names such as `...git`.
findings.trigger: A header with `job_id: ".."`.

findings.title: `info.git_sha` can report an unrelated repository's HEAD
findings.detail: `git -C <site-packages>/nightwright rev-parse HEAD` walks up the directory tree. For a `uv tool install`, this reports the HEAD of whatever git repo contains the tool directory (for example, a home directory tracked as a dotfiles repo), not nightwright's own commit.
findings.trigger: The worker user's home directory, or any parent of `~/.local/share/uv/tools`, is a git work tree.

findings.title: After a cancel, a frame write gives up after one 0.5 s unwritable select, leaving a half-written line and no `done`
findings.detail: In `_Frames._write_fd`, once `cancel` is set (stdin EOF or a signal), the first `select` that times out after 0.5 s sets `closed=True` and returns. A frame that was partly written in PIPE_BUF pieces stays on stdout as a truncated JSON line. Every later frame, including the `done` with `interrupted: true` that the spec says is sent "if it can", is then dropped, even though the coordinator is still reading. The process still exits 0, so the coordinator gets exit 0 with a broken last line and no `done`. That contradicts "gate-job never exits without one of the two frames unless stdout is closed".
findings.trigger: The coordinator cancels by closing stdin (or SIGTERM arrives) while a multi-MiB `gate` frame is being written, and the coordinator's read side pauses for more than 0.5 s, for example a full SSH channel window on a slow link.

findings.title: A pre-slot signal does not interrupt a wait on the repo flock
findings.detail: Before the slot stage the signal handler only records the signal unless the job is blocked reading stdin. `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` in `repo_lock` is retried after EINTR (PEP 475), so a job waiting for the repo lock ignores SIGTERM/SIGHUP until the holder releases it. The holder may be another job's slow fetch or a `git gc --prune=now` on a big cache, so the job can outlive the connection by minutes.
findings.trigger: Job A's checkout waits on `repos/<key>.lock` while gc prunes a large cache, and sshd or the coordinator sends SIGTERM/SIGHUP to job A.

findings.title: `nw worker have` turns a git failure into a traceback
findings.detail: `have()` calls `_set_have`, which uses `_git(..., check=True)`. A failing `update-ref` (disk full, an unwritable ref) raises `WorkerError`, but `worker_have` only catches `ValueError`. Over SSH the coordinator gets a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1, not a clean error.
findings.trigger: `update-ref refs/nw/have/<sha>` fails in the cache during `nw worker have --repo K <sha>`.

findings.title: `info.git_sha` can report an unrelated repository
findings.detail: `git -C <site-packages>/nightwright rev-parse HEAD` searches up the directory tree. In a `uv tool install` under a home directory that is itself a git repo (dotfiles), it reports that repo's HEAD as nightwright's `git_sha`.
findings.trigger: The worker user's home or one of its parent directories is a git work tree.
